Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No.2585 of 2023
Anurag ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Ms. Meena Bisht, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. M.A. Khan, A.G.A. for the State.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Applicant Anurag is in judicial custody in Case Crime No. 122 of 2023, under Section 363, 376 Ipc
and Section 3(a)/4 (1) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station
Patel Nagar, District Dehradun.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the applicant enticed the victim, a young girl of 16 years on 10.03.2022 and established physical relation with her.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant and the victim, both are in relationship, therefore, the victim joined the company of the applicant.
She would submit that it is so stated by the victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

5. Learned State counsel would submit that the victim was a child, but she has supported the prosecution case at trial.
6.

In the cases of Mahesh Kumar v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine Del 2634, Faizan Wahid Baig v. The State of Maharashtra, MANU/MHOR/62774/2022, Vijaylakshmi and another v. State and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Mad 317, Shri John Franklin Shylla v. State of Meghalaya & Anr.,
2023 SCC OnLine Megh 303 and Ashik Ramjali Ansari v. State of Maharashtra and another, 2023 SCC OnLine Bom 1390, the Courts have either granted bail or quashed the proceedings or acquitted the accused in the cases like instant one.
7. Having considered, this Court is of the view that subject to certain conditions, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text:
9. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant or any of his relatives shall not make any contact with the victim, in any manner, whatsoever, either physically, electronically or by any other means.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing the facts to Court or any Police Officer and the applicant should not tamper with evidence.

(Ravindra Maithani, J) 15.05.2024 Jitendra Anurag vs State Of Uttarakhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145189978/
